location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin (Sahelian zone), four countries
subsector_stated: Training and information component: training extension workers and farmers in IPM techniques
intervention_stated: Training in IPM techniques of trainers and farmers in Farmer Field Schools; training took place five to six months before the crop season
rationale_stated: Acquisition by farmers of skills enabling them to adopt and apply IPM techniques; knowledge should be a decisive factor in creating conditions for survival of the system beyond the funding period
result_stated: Technical guidance through village brigades of 6 farmers per village, trained in basic plant protection techniques (total: 120 farmers, of which 29 women, i.e. 24%); rate of pilot farmer participation in FFS activities at least 80%
result_unit: pilot farmers trained in Farmer Field Schools
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation document review; PCU survey; field visits to 13 villages including 10 pilot villages

location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Impact on gender; women play a special role in food security in the region
intervention_stated: Training of women pilot farmers in Farmer Field Schools; women extension workers facilitated the active participation of rural pilot women farmers
rationale_stated: Women contribute significantly to food production, processing and marketing but lack access to key inputs (land, credit, agricultural equipment) and training
result_stated: Women represented 24% of pilot farmers (29 women out of 120) trained in Farmer Field Schools; their participation in FFS activities was highly satisfactory, averaging above 70%; at least 20% of extension workers trained were women
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation document review and beneficiary interviews

location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Adoption and use of IPM techniques by farmers
intervention_stated: Training and supervision of farmers through the village brigades: adoption of new farming methods, identification of major insect pests and diseases, mastery of neem extraction and spraying techniques, conservation of useful insects
rationale_stated: Provide farmers the tools to analyse their own practices and identify specific solutions to the problems they face (Farmer Field School approach)
result_stated: Regular weeding and seed treatment were applied most by pilot farmers in their own fields, adoption rates respectively 89% and 88%, followed by thinning (79%), row seeding (78%) and pre-planting soil preparation; pre-planting seed germination test least adopted (20%)
result_unit: % adoption rate of regular weeding by pilot farmers (highest-adopted technique)
evidence_stated: PCU survey of over 600 farmers in the 20 pilot villages and surrounding villages within a 10 km radius, December 2004

location_names: 20 pilot villages and surrounding villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Testing and regional coordination of IPM techniques; extension through Farmer Field Schools and demonstration plots
intervention_stated: Almost 500 Farmer Field School days and 600 visits to demonstration plots established in pilot farmers' fields were organized each year (2003 and 2004)
rationale_stated: Ensure the extension of IPM in the four countries involved through the Farmer Field School approach
result_stated: Through the application of IPM techniques, nearly ten thousand (10 000) farm managers (compared to one thousand envisaged at project start-up) were able to increase their yields of subsistence crops (millet, sorghum, cowpea); each pilot farmer contacted by 24 other farmers on average
result_unit: farm managers able to increase yields of subsistence crops through IPM application
evidence_stated: PCU survey of over 600 farmers in pilot and surrounding villages (Dec 2004); external impact assessment by IITA (Dec 2004)

location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Use of neem-based botanical insecticides in integrated pest management
intervention_stated: Introduction of neem-based botanical insecticide (powder, aqueous extracts and oil); pilot farmers mastered techniques of production, formulation, application and storage
rationale_stated: Reduce farmers' dependence on chemical pesticides that are costly and harmful to human health and the environment
result_stated: Use of neem-based botanical insecticide is now common among pilot farmers; nearly 90% of farmers found these products effective against stem borers, defoliating caterpillars and aphids; over 70% of producers find them readily available and inexpensive
result_unit: % of farmers finding neem-based botanical insecticides effective against major pests
evidence_stated: PCU survey of over 600 farmers in pilot and surrounding villages, December 2004; field visits

location_names: Farmer Field Schools in 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Reduction of pest-related crop losses through IPM techniques
intervention_stated: Application of IPM techniques against Striga hermonthica attacks on sorghum; use of neem extracts against stem borers; seed treatment with Apron Star 42WS
rationale_stated: Striga hermonthica is capable of damaging over 60% of production; pest-related crop losses of up to 50%
result_stated: The project has helped to fight against Striga hermonthica attacks on sorghum; infestation reduced from 60 to 100% in Farmer Field Schools compared to control plots; neem extracts provided effective protection against insects such as stem borers
result_unit: % reduction of Striga hermonthica infestation on sorghum, FFS vs control plots
evidence_stated: Field trials; tracking plot counts per square meter according to site, FFS vs control plots

location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Impact on poverty reduction; project particularly geared towards smallholders and subsistence farming
intervention_stated: Application of IPM techniques on a standard 2-ha farm based on sorghum (1 ha), cowpea (0.5 ha) and millet (0.5 ha)
rationale_stated: Project tested cost-effective technologies adapted to the environment and aimed at reducing pest-related losses
result_stated: Annual income rose from CFAF 146,600 in the pre-project situation to CFAF 408,100 with the project; increase estimated at CFAF 261,500 against CFAF 130,000 forecast at appraisal; valuation of family labour rose from CFAF 586/day to CFAF 1626/day (+177%)
result_unit: CFAF increase in annual income per standard 2-ha farm
evidence_stated: Standard farm model comparing pre-project and with-project situations; PCR estimates validated by the evaluation

location_names: 20 pilot villages, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Economic benefits of IPM application at farm level
intervention_stated: Application of IPM techniques substituting imported chemical pesticides with neem extracts and biological control
rationale_stated: Chemical pesticides are extremely costly; foreign exchange savings by replacing imported chemicals with IPM method
result_stated: The production value generated with the application of IPM techniques is estimated at CFAF 1 billion; member countries have realized savings of around CFAF 2 billion with the use of neem extracts
result_unit: CFAF production value generated with application of IPM techniques
evidence_stated: Extrapolation of income at the level of budgets of LCBC member states; PCR estimates

location_names: Project area, Lake Chad Basin, four countries
subsector_stated: Training and information; dissemination through simple, pictorial and adapted publications
intervention_stated: Production of IPM training manuals and brochures; a guide to IPM menus for each major crop (millet, sorghum, rain-fed cowpea); two posters, one on Striga and one on use of neem powder against stalk borers
rationale_stated: To sustain training activities and foster dissemination of IPM techniques
result_stated: IPM guides for technicians and farmers prepared, plus an IPM manual; two posters prepared; documents translated into four languages spoken in the area (Arabic, Fulfulde, Hausa, Kanuri); guides and brochures were not widely circulated due to printer's failure
result_unit: local languages into which IPM guides, manuals and posters were translated
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation document review

location_names: Ngala (LCBC Regional Agricultural Training School), Nigeria
subsector_stated: Capacity building for LCBC in training, through the LCBC Regional Agricultural Training School in Ngala, Nigeria
intervention_stated: Enhancing the capacity of the LCBC Regional School in Ngala by providing equipment, teaching materials and training courses on IPM technological packages; seminar on integrated pest management organized for students
rationale_stated: Strengthen the Ngala Regional School to support member countries in enhancing their pest management capacity in subsistence farming
result_stated: The Ngala Regional School equipped with the required materials (operational); it has also benefited from training in IPM; capacity building activities implemented: 70 students
result_unit: students trained at the Ngala Regional School
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation document review; retrospective logical framework matrix

subsector_stated: Production and marketing of neem-based products as a source of income for farmers
intervention_stated: Use of neem-based products introduced by the project; production, formulation, application and storage techniques mastered by pilot farmers
rationale_stated: The use of neem-based products opened new opportunities for farmers; neem production can generate income for farmers planning to engage in this activity
result_stated: In the villages of Shehuri and Abbar in Nigeria, some farmers produce and sell these products on the local market
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation field visits, October 2009

subsector_stated: Full-scale implementation of IPM techniques in farmers' fields, notably organic manure and chemical fertilizers
intervention_stated: IPM techniques demonstrated on 900 m2 (30x30) demonstration plots; use of inputs (organic manure, chemical fertilizers) in pilot farmers' fields
rationale_stated: Due to lack of sufficient resources, farmers make limited use of inputs; one hectare requires at least CFAF 82,500 of manure, excluding transportation costs
result_stated: Farmers have developed an original strategy, which is to allow the Arab shepherds in transhumance to pen animals in their fields in exchange for two kilogrammes of sugar
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation field visits and beneficiary interviews, October 2009

subsector_stated: Use of neem extracts for crop protection under IPM
intervention_stated: IPM training and use of neem extracts introduced in the pilot village through Farmer Field Schools and village brigades
rationale_stated: Neem is a non-chemical, environmentally-friendly and cost-effective alternative to synthetic pesticides
result_stated: Farmers of Mandjafa and Klessum believe that neem is less effective than chemical insecticides, even though they acknowledge the adverse effects on humans and the environment; they all agreed they derive much benefit from using neem in crop protection, production and income
evidence_stated: Ex-post evaluation interviews with beneficiaries in 13 villages visited, October 2009

subsector_stated: Crop insurance as a risk management tool; tailored agricultural insurance products including Area Yield Index, Weather Index and Livestock mortality cover
intervention_stated: ACRE Rwanda designing and distributing tailored agricultural insurance products since 2014; upscaling intervention from 2019 to improve existing insurance products under the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS)
rationale_stated: Farming is fraught with unpredictability due to pests, diseases, and adverse weather; crop insurance emerges as a critical risk management tool, protecting farmers against economic losses and providing a financial safety net
result_stated: There has been a significant uptake in the adoption of these products, particularly among those who participated in the program; higher rate of engagement and adoption
evidence_stated: Qualitative impact assessment by independent consultants for SCBF; four focus group discussions with 33 smallholder farmers (23 women, 10 men)

location_names: Rwamagana and Ngoma districts (Kohunya and Imberutso za Karembo Cooperatives)
subsector_stated: Financial education around insurance and other financial concepts for farmers
intervention_stated: Financial Education (FE) program: insurance product training and financial education delivered through ToTs and cooperative meetings, with gender-sensitive measures, to increase uptake of insurance products among Rwandan farmers
rationale_stated: The main barriers hindering the uptake and use of financial services are affordability and lack of awareness; financial education has transformative potential in increasing the uptake of insurance products among Rwandan farmers
result_stated: A substantial 85.7% of farmers attended 1 to 5 financial education programs in the past year, with a strong consensus (71.4%) agreeing that such training significantly improves their understanding of financial products and services
result_unit: % of farmers attending financial education programs
evidence_stated: Four focus group discussions engaging 33 smallholder farmers (23 women, 10 men), aged 23-69, from Rwamagana and Ngoma districts; qualitative analysis by independent consultants

subsector_stated: maize crop insurance
intervention_stated: Kilimo Salama Project pilot season (October 2012 to March 2013) focused predominantly on maize crop insurance, funded by SFSA, Access to Finance Rwanda and MINAGRI.
rationale_stated: The project sought to evaluate the feasibility of offering crop and livestock insurance products tailored to Rwanda's unique agricultural ecosystem.
result_stated: In its pilot season from October 2012 to March 2013, the Kilimo Salama Project focused predominantly on maize crop insurance and was able to onboard 20,000 farmers.
evidence_stated: Project background narrative in the impact assessment report citing historical programme records

subsector_stated: crop and livestock insurance products
intervention_stated: Kilimo Salama Project sale of agricultural insurance, evolving from maize crop insurance to introduce livestock insurance in 2014.
rationale_stated: Evaluate the feasibility of offering crop and livestock insurance products tailored to Rwanda's unique agricultural ecosystem.
result_stated: Despite setbacks due to basis risk in subsequent years in some ecological zones, the project sold more than 120,000 policies over a period of four years.
evidence_stated: Project background narrative in the impact assessment report citing historical programme records

location_names: Rwanda (national; emphasis on Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western Provinces and Kigali City)
subsector_stated: agricultural insurance and financial literacy
intervention_stated: 2019 ACRE Africa initiative funded by SCBF to upscale existing insurance products and launch financial literacy campaigns, adopting a blended approach.
rationale_stated: Aiming to offer an invaluable safety net to smallholder farmers and address the financial literacy gap in the agricultural value chain.

subsector_stated: training sessions related to crop insurance, weather, and climate information
intervention_stated: Training sessions for smallholder farmers on crop insurance, weather and climate information, delivered through outreach initiatives since 2019.
rationale_stated: Outreach initiatives targeted at smallholder farmers contributing to increased awareness and potentially greater adoption of insurance products.
result_stated: Reported attendance figures for smallholder farmers in training sessions overwhelmingly indicating participation of over 10,000 individuals in such programs.
evidence_stated: Key informant interviews with 15 stakeholder institutions via structured questionnaire 'Impact assessment KII_ACRESCBF' (purposive sampling); attendance figures as reported by respondents

intervention_stated: Capacity building, training and technical support provided to industry professionals and stakeholders in the agriculture insurance sector since 2019.
rationale_stated: To gauge how these sessions might have contributed to the acceptance and adoption of agricultural insurance products.
evidence_stated: KII questionnaire of 15 respondents; respondent shares of training attendance (40% none, 40% one to five sessions, 13% more than eleven) are survey-sample percentages, not beneficiary counts

result_stated: A single respondent reported that their company sold fewer than 5,000 policies to smallholder farmers since the program's inception in 2019.
result_unit: policies sold to smallholder farmers (fewer than; one company)

rationale_stated: Some companies have been remarkably successful in reaching a broad swath of the smallholder farming community.
result_stated: Two respondents indicated that their companies sold over 20,001 policies during the same period (since the program's inception in 2019).
result_unit: policies sold (over; each of two companies)

subsector_stated: Area Yield Index insurance
intervention_stated: Area Yield Index product compensating insured farmers if the actual yield of a specified crop in a defined area falls below a predetermined threshold; government-run, using crop cut to assess yield shortfalls.
rationale_stated: Its popularity underscores the volatility of yields and the inherent risks of farming in certain regions.
evidence_stated: KII responses on products offered (response shares are respondent proportions, not adoption figures)

subsector_stated: Weather Index insurance
intervention_stated: Weather Index product protecting farmers against deviations from established weather benchmarks which could adversely affect crop output.
rationale_stated: Its adoption indicates the significant role that unpredictable weather patterns play in farming activities, particularly in the face of global climate change.
evidence_stated: KII responses on products offered (response shares are respondent proportions, not adoption figures)

subsector_stated: Livestock Mortality Cover
intervention_stated: Livestock Mortality Cover protecting farmers against unexpected livestock deaths.
rationale_stated: Protecting against unexpected livestock deaths is of paramount concern for many farmers, emphasizing the role livestock plays in their livelihood.
evidence_stated: KII responses on products offered (response shares are respondent proportions, not adoption figures)

subsector_stated: insurance products
intervention_stated: Agricultural insurance products marketed to farmers in the Eastern Province.
rationale_stated: The region has a semi-dry climate and lower altitude, making it more prone to climatic adversities and crop production risks, suggesting greater receptivity to risk mitigation initiatives.
result_stated: The Eastern Province demonstrates the highest uptake of insurance products among farmers.
evidence_stated: Key informant interviews with 15 stakeholder institutions; geographic distribution of uptake as reported by respondents

subsector_stated: insurance products
intervention_stated: Agricultural insurance products marketed to farmers in the Southern Province.
rationale_stated: Shares some biophysical attributes with the Eastern Province, such as lower altitude and greater risks for crop production.
result_stated: The Southern Province follows closely (gaining momentum in insurance uptake).
evidence_stated: Key informant interviews with 15 stakeholder institutions; geographic distribution of uptake as reported by respondents

subsector_stated: insurance products; insurance cover
intervention_stated: Agricultural insurance products marketed in the Northern and Western Provinces, with sustained effort being deployed to reverse low subscription following catastrophic floods and landslides.
rationale_stated: These regions may be seeing lower interest because they are less prone to drought and crop failures due to their cooler and wet climates; targeted strategic interventions in these areas are crucial.
result_stated: Northern and Western Provinces have less traction in terms of insurance product uptake; most of farmers in these regions had not subscribed to any form of insurance cover.
evidence_stated: Key informant interviews with 15 stakeholder institutions; geographic distribution of uptake as reported by respondents

subsector_stated: value chains like rice farming
intervention_stated: Agricultural insurance as a risk mitigation tool applied in crop value chains, particularly rice farming.
rationale_stated: The power of insurance as a risk mitigation tool, particularly evident during disasters such as the recent catastrophic floods and landslides.
result_stated: In over all, the major benefit has been especially impactful in value chains like rice farming, saving partners from losses.
evidence_stated: Key informant interviews with 15 stakeholder institutions; qualitative lessons-learned responses

location_names: South West Indian Ocean region (SWIOFC member countries)
subsector_stated: Management effectiveness of selected priority fisheries at regional level; tuna and tuna-like fisheries
intervention_stated: Enhanced regional collaboration: regional Minimum Terms and Conditions for access to tuna fishery, joint fisheries MCS activities, regional tuna strategy, SWIOFC sustainable financing mechanism, and technical advice and studies informing fisheries agreements
rationale_stated: An estimated 28 percent of regional fish stocks overexploited or depleted; annual economic rent loss of US$225 million; regional cooperation seen as key given the shared marine ecosystem
result_stated: Eleven bilateral fisheries agreements signed by SWIOFC member countries (target six); MTC guidelines for foreign fisheries access adopted 2018; regional financing mechanism agreed 2019; eight joint tuna resolutions adopted by IOTC
evidence_stated: Results framework indicator monitoring; IOC completion report

location_names: Comoros (national; Anjouan, Grande Comore, Moheli islands)
subsector_stated: Demersal and pelagic coastal fisheries; priority fisheries: tuna, demersal fisheries, lobster, sea cucumber
intervention_stated: Evaluation and expansion of 2013 Demersal Fisheries Management Plan into a National Coastal Fisheries Management Plan; vessel registration system design, computerized registration database, registration campaigns in the three islands, construction of a fisheries monitoring center
rationale_stated: Most coastal fisheries under heavy pressure; weak legal and institutional framework, human capacity, and infrastructure resulted in deficient management of small-scale fisheries
result_stated: National Coastal Fisheries Management Plan adopted December 2020, partially implemented: 2,104 of 3,000 vessels registered (67 percent), 19 vessels licensed in 2021; fisheries monitoring center built, equipped, and made functional
evidence_stated: PDO-level results framework indicator; borrower completion report

subsector_stated: Control of fishing activity; monitoring, control, and surveillance (MCS)
